holidays.name: National Popcorn Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the fluffy, crunchy snack that explodes into existence when heated. Pop a big bowl, drizzle it with butter, and get creative with flavors like caramel, cheddar, or even chili-lime.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday observed in the United States, popularized through food-holiday calendars. Popcorn itself has been eaten in the Americas for thousands of years, with ancient kernels found in Peruvian and Mexican archaeological sites.
holidays.funFact: Popcorn pops because each kernel contains a droplet of water inside a hard starchy shell. When heated to about 350°F, the steam builds pressure until the kernel bursts, and popcorn was reportedly the first food ever cooked in a microwave on purpose in experiments in the 1940s.

holidays.name: National Tin Can Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble tin can, the pantry hero that keeps soup, beans, and tuna fresh for ages. Celebrate by cracking open a can of something and appreciating the miracle of food preservation.
holidays.origin: Commemorates January 19, 1825, when Thomas Kensett patented the tin can in the United States. The date is marked as the anniversary of that patent.
holidays.funFact: The tin can was invented decades before the can opener. Early cans were so thick that people had to open them with a hammer and chisel, or even by shooting them, until the can opener arrived around 1858.

holidays.name: National Rubber Duckie Day
holidays.description: A bubbly celebration of the squeaky yellow bath companion that has judged our soaking sessions for generations. Bring one to the tub, the desk, or the dashboard of your car.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially on January 13 in some calendars, but many rubber duck fans and calendars celebrate the duckie around mid-to-late January, tying it to the toy's widespread bath-time fame. Its popularity soared after Sesame Street's Ernie sang 'Rubber Duckie' in 1970.
holidays.funFact: In 1992, a shipping container of about 28,800 rubber ducks and other bath toys fell off a cargo ship into the Pacific Ocean, and the toys have since drifted around the world, helping oceanographers study ocean currents.

holidays.name: Edgar Allan Poe Day
holidays.description: A moody, raven-filled celebration of the master of the macabre on his birthday. Fans read 'The Raven' aloud, sip something dark and mysterious, and tip a hat to the father of the detective story.
holidays.origin: Edgar Allan Poe was born on January 19, 1809, in Boston, Massachusetts. Literary fans and Poe societies celebrate his birthday each year.
holidays.funFact: For decades, a mysterious stranger known as the 'Poe Toaster' visited Poe's grave in Baltimore every January 19 before dawn, leaving three roses and a half-empty bottle of cognac. The tradition ended in 2010.
